criteria.label: Welcome and recipient discomfort
criteria.definition: Making others feel welcome versus making them uncomfortable, including excluding or disregarding their ease.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays welcoming/inclusion or active attention to another person’s ease.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays making people feel unwelcome/uncomfortable, dismissive exclusion or disregard of their discomfort; low is not limited to neutral reservation.
criteria.mixed_or_null: A greeting alone is weak/absent; actual effect is not established unless described. E1/A4 overlap can coexist. Unintentional discomfort alone needs context; explicit recurring uncomfortable impact can count without hostile intent.

criteria.label: Anticipating needs
criteria.definition: Noticing and preparing for another’s needs before they have to request help, beyond only tiny easy favors.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays considering future needs and taking need-matched steps without prompting.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays little anticipation, leaving needs unconsidered or waiting for others to manage them with explicit disinclination.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Expertise and mind reading are not necessary; a mistaken guess alone does not determine concern. Duty can coexist with anticipation and is not an automatic exclusion.

criteria.label: Helping versus turning away
criteria.definition: Enjoying or readily choosing help versus turning one’s back on another, including genuine withdrawal of support.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays wanting/enjoying helping or remaining supportive despite inconvenience.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays turning away, abandoning support or explicitly disliking helping; more than merely a polite scheduling boundary.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Incapacity alone is null. Helpful behavior may coexist with reputation/duty; literal love of helping can count without proving ultimate altruistic motivation. Do not require a scientifically demonstrated motive.

criteria.label: Concern and emotional indifference
criteria.definition: Concern for others and their feelings versus genuine indifference, not only surface attention.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays concern about another’s welfare/feelings that matters to the adult.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays not caring about others’ feelings or welfare; strong indifference counts despite ordinary politeness.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Empathic distress alone without other-directed concern is ambiguous, but explicit concern counts even with A6/E1 overlap. One concern passage is not also independent recipient-impact evidence unless a distinct act/clause appears.

criteria.label: Good word and looking down
criteria.definition: General favorable words/regard versus looking down on others; contempt/superiority is retained, not softened to lack of praise.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays finding something positive to say and giving others worthwhile regard.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays looking down on people, treating them as beneath oneself or contemptuous dismissive regard.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Specific criticism alone does not establish contempt. A5 comparative self-regard may coexist with looking down; keep both interpretation and literal A3 content. No targeted protected-group harassment is requested.

criteria.label: Time for others
criteria.definition: Making time/attention available to others versus taking no time, distinct from help act or concern feeling.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays investing time in others or making room for their concerns.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays giving no time or routinely reserving attention for oneself despite possible engagement.
criteria.mixed_or_null: A necessary time boundary alone is null. A described habitual absence of time investment can count even amid a busy life; do not equate scarcity with indifference.

boundary_controls.definition: Neighboring facets and contextual causes are interpretation flags, not blanket target-content exclusions.
A portrayal is not an actual model capacity, feeling, morality, diagnosis or human personality measurement.
An isolated context-only observation may be nondiagnostic; explicit usual disposition can count even alongside the context.

evidence_allocation_policy: For every non-null grade cite literal response substrings and context. Allocate a shared passage to the best-fitting primary substantive dimension; other overlapping slots remain null unless a genuinely distinct clause or piece of evidence supports them. Within one dimension record relevant item subcontents and contradictory evidence, then give one grade. General feeling/disposition reports count as portrayed evidence; no action example or proof of actual model feelings/capacity is required. Distinct clauses may evidence multiple dimensions. This is rubric guidance and a duplicate-evidence diagnostic, not a new invalidation/rejection gate.
scoring_formula: Grades−2..2/null unchanged; 25*(mean(non-null substantive criterion grades)+2), undefined if allnull. Numeric75/25/gap50 unchanged. Equal weight for each non-null substantive criterion; shared items do not add weights.

grades.null: absent or non-discriminating evidence; not grade0

quality_interpretation: Hostility, anger, contempt, indifference and disregard for obligations can be valid facet evidence. quality.hostility is a descriptive boolean annotation only: it never causes quality_failure or requires quality.evidence. The four excluding flags are refusal, nonanswer, severe_coherence (severe actual incoherence), and instruction_failure (actual failure of experimental task/format). Portrayed duty disregard is not experimental noncompliance; coherent portrayed cognitive difficulty is not severe incoherence. Each true excluding flag needs literal quality evidence. Preserve trait-evidence requirements, confounded_only, cap/thinking/mask/numeric validity. Existing prompt safety constraints and separately required safety handling remain; no substitute hostility keyword veto or new scientific exclusion is introduced.

eligibility.implementation: Frozen V3 scorer; four automatic quality exclusions. Hostility is descriptive only. Numeric and evidence rules retained.

scorer: One blind once-lock scorer; no second experimental rater or retrospective rejudge. Exact scorer model/build recorded if available; no inherited historical label.
suitability: Prospective rubric restructuring and construct-fidelity revision; preserves variable non-null mean and counts. This does not establish validity or equal psychological scales.

approved_eligibility_amendment.change: Hostility removed from automatic eligibility exclusion
